commits.message:
fix(box): leave an already-ASCII box alone under asciiOnly (rich-table-0gv)

`substitute({ asciiOnly: true })` answered `ASCII` for every box, including
the four that are already pure ASCII. A MARKDOWN table on a terminal without
unicode silently became a plus-and-pipe frame instead of the pipe-delimited
markdown it was chosen for; ASCII2 and ASCII_DOUBLE_HEAD were erased the same
way. The reference guards with "if options.ascii_only and not box.ascii".

Whether a box is drawable without unicode is derived from its grid at
construction, not declared per constant as the reference's `ascii=True` is.
A `Box` is wholly its grid, so the grid already answers this and a second
hand-written answer could disagree with it — and derivation reaches boxes no
constant speaks for: `safeSubstitute` builds a fresh `Box` from an edited
grid, and a flag on the shipped constants would say nothing about that one.
The predicate names exactly the four the reference constructs with
`ascii=True`, pinned by naming all nineteen in the test rather than asserting
the count.

This also fixes, with no change to table.ts, an asciiOnly + headerless
ASCII_DOUBLE_HEAD table. `Table.render` runs the two box swaps in the
reference's order, so `substitute` handing the box through unchanged leaves
`plainHeaded` a box it recognises: the frame is now ASCII2's crossed edge
("+---+---+") as Rich draws it, where replacing the box first left
`plainHeaded` holding ASCII and an uncrossed "+-------+".

Verified: six of the seven new assertions are red against the previous
box.ts. 2335 pass, three-pass lint and demo typecheck clean, golden files
unmoved.

fix(table): stamp the header and footer on assignment, not at the constructor (rich-table-n8a) (#105)

`toCellText` is the one crossing where caller content becomes table content,
and it makes three promises: markup is parsed, `end` is cleared because a cell
is a fragment rather than a line, and a `RichText` is copied so the caller no
longer owns the table's cell. `Column`'s constructor kept all three.

Nothing kept them after it. `Table.columns` hands out the live array and both
fields were plain and public, so an assignment landed unstamped in a slot every
reader below assumes the crossing has been through:

    const mine = new RichText("Foot");
    t.columns[0].footer = mine;   // no copy, no parse, `end` intact
    mine.append("MUTATED");       // and the table's footer changes with it

The invariant was established in a constructor and violable for the rest of the
object's life, which makes the stamp a convention the constructor happened to
follow rather than something the type proves.

Both fields are now accessor pairs whose setters route through `toCellText`, so
there is exactly one writer of the backing field in the program and the
constructor is one caller of the border rather than the one place it is true —
the same shape `Layout` already uses for `ratio` and `minimumSize`, which had
this bug for the same reason. `readonly` was the other candidate and is weaker
twice over: it is erased at runtime, and it would delete a capability the
reference has, where `Column` is a mutable dataclass. Assignment stays legal and
now parses markup too, because it crosses the same door construction does.

The setters take `undefined` rather than defaulting around it: absent and empty
are already the same header, and `toCellText` is where that mapping lives.

`copy()` stopped copying its own header and footer on the way into the
constructor — the crossing there copies a `RichText` already, and a second copy
is a second home for one rule. The existing "copy creates independent instance"
test grew the mutation assertion that makes that checkable.

The two `end` frames in the ticket do not reproduce, and the tests pin what is
observable instead: `_renderRow` justifies the cell to `cellWidth` before `end`
is appended and `adjustLineLength` crops it straight back off, so a header's or
footer's `end` never reaches the frame at any width or justification. The stamp
is asserted on the field; the copy and the markup parse are asserted through the
rendered output. Eight new tests, all red without this change.

2314 pass, `table-frames.golden.txt` unmoved and untouched, three-pass lint and
the demo typecheck clean.
